article.title: Tired of 'git clone' just for one file? Meet ghgrab!
article.body_markdown:
---
title: Tired of 'git clone' just for one file? Meet ghgrab!
published: True
tags: cli, github, gitlab, developertools
---

## Quick Summary: 📝
ghgrab is a command-line interface tool built with Rust that allows users to browse and download specific files or folders from various Git forges like GitHub, GitLab, and others directly from their terminal. It features a user-friendly TUI for easy navigation, file preview, and efficient selection, avoiding the need for full repository clones.

## Key Takeaways: 💡

* ✅ ghgrab is a CLI tool for browsing and downloading specific files or folders from Git forges without cloning the entire repository.

* ✅ It features an intuitive Terminal User Interface (TUI) for a smooth and interactive browsing experience.

* ✅ Supports GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, Gitea, and Forgejo, with features like fuzzy search, file preview, and GitHub LFS support.

* ✅ Easy to install across different ecosystems (NPM, Cargo, pipx) and offers specialized functions like GitHub repository discovery and release artifact downloads.

* ✅ Significantly enhances developer productivity by eliminating the 'clone-and-delete' workflow and saving time.


## Project Statistics: 📊
* ⭐ **Stars:** 1573
* 🍴 **Forks:** 89
* ❗ **Open Issues:** 3


## Tech Stack: 💻
- ✅ Rust


Ever found yourself needing just one tiny configuration file, a specific script, or a single asset from a massive GitHub repository? You probably sighed, typed 'git clone', waited for the entire repo to download, then painstakingly navigated to the file, copied it, and finally deleted the whole cloned directory. It's a common developer chore, and frankly, it's inefficient. What if I told you there's a fantastic new tool that lets you 'grab anything you want' from GitHub, GitLab, and other popular Git forges, all without ever leaving your terminal or downloading more than you need?
Enter ghgrab, a sleek and powerful command-line interface tool that's about to become your new best friend for repository exploration. Built with the speed and safety of Rust, leveraging the tokio and ratatui ecosystems, ghgrab provides a beautiful Terminal User Interface (TUI). This isn't just a basic text interface; it's a fully interactive experience that makes browsing repositories feel incredibly smooth and intuitive. You can navigate through folders, preview source code, and cherry-pick exactly the files or directories you need with ease. It's like having a miniature web browser for Git repositories right in your CLI, but hyper-focused on efficiency.
The benefits of integrating ghgrab into your workflow are immediate and substantial. First and foremost, it eliminates the 'clone-and-delete' dance, saving you precious time and bandwidth. Need a file? Just ghgrab it! The clean TUI ensures that browsing is not only fast but also a pleasure to use. Installation is a breeze, whether you're a JavaScript aficionado (NPM), a Rustacean (Cargo), or a Pythonista (pipx), ghgrab has you covered. Beyond simple file grabbing, ghgrab is packed with features. You can quickly search and navigate through any repo's folders using fuzzy search, making it super easy to find what you're looking for. It even has built-in repository discovery, allowing you to search GitHub directly from the home screen. For those dealing with larger assets, ghgrab boasts support for GitHub LFS (Large File Storage), and you can even download multiple files and folders in batch mode. A particularly useful feature is its ability to download GitHub release artifacts, intelligently selecting the best match for your operating system and architecture. This project truly is a game-changer for anyone who frequently interacts with Git repositories from the command line.
Imagine the time saved, the cleaner directories, and the sheer convenience. ghgrab is more than just a downloader; it's a productivity enhancer that respects your time and your terminal. Go check it out on GitHub, give it a star, and integrate it into your daily toolkit. You won't regret it!
